newsitem.title: UK: Mideast and Far Eastern clean tanker rates soften.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and Far Eastern clean tanker rates soften.

text.p: The absence of enquiries for clean tankers in the Middle East caused rates to slide and levels to both eastern and western destinations declined, brokers said.
E.A. Gibson said in a report that levels for long-haul voyages to the Far East declined to W212.5 for the 33,000 tonne size.
Brokers said 20,000 tonne inter U.K./Cont business fell back to W225 from last week's W230
"In the Mediterranean, the clean products market struggled to maintain last week's levels with barely sufficient enquiry to employ available tonnage," E.A. Gibson said.
Naphtha liftings remained at W280 basis the usual 27,500-tonne cargo in the cross-Med trade. Other clean oil products obtained between W240 and W250 for both cross-Med and Black Sea to Med voyages.

"Numerous charterers tried in vain to secure tonnage suitable for the transportation of jet from this are to the East, but there were few owners able to accommodate charterers' ideas of $1.1 million basis 40,000 tonnes of cargo," the report said.
The holidays in Venezuela restricted clean trades from the area in the early part of the week, forcing some upcoast rates to fall below W290 while larger 40,000 tonne cargoes closed at W212.5.
Fixtures were relatively steady in the U.K./Cont market on strong enquiries. Gas oil stems of 25,000/26,000 tonnes from the Baltic paid around W210 for U.K./Cont discharge.
